 Judgment

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Ramaiah.S in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.11.2022.
2.

The case of the petitioner, in brief, is as follows:
Shivaraju.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30325063/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 05.11.2022 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Ramaiah.S, was crossing the road from the road divider in the direction of west, a KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA 40 F1255, was coming from Bengaluru side towards Devanahalli side in the direction of south to north.
At that time the said KSRTC bus was driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life which came and hit the pedestrian Sri.Ramaiah.S.

Due to the force impact of the SCCH4 3 MVC No.6617/2022 road accident, the deceased was taken to Life Care Hospital, which is situated near by the place of accident wherein the doctor declared that deceased is no more.

Immediately after the accident, the dead body was shifted to Government Hospital,
Yelahanka wherein post mortem was conducted on 06.11.2022 and petitioners have spent huge amount towards funeral obsequies and funeral expenses etc.,.
The deceased was contributing the same to his family maintenance but due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioner has lost love and affection and care taker.
The deceased is the brother of petitioner.
Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy he was doing the work of MasonSupervisor/Gaare Mesthri and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month.
SCCH4 4 MVC No.6617/2022
The respondent is the owner and there is internal insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest.
3. The respondent has entered appearance through its advocate and filed objection statement by denying the claim of the petitioner.

Further contended that, the vehicle of the respondent bearing Reg.No.KA40F1255, on 05.11.2022, around 7.15 p.m. while traveling from Bangalore to Chikkaballapura near Sadalli Toll, the deceased Ramaiah abruptly crossed over the divider.
The bus driver immediately applied the brakes and tried to take the bus to left side, however the deceased Ramaiah.S immediately reversed course and rushed back, stricking the bus in the process.
The driver had no influence over the accidents circumstances.
The accident was beyond the control of the driver hence, the driver is not responsible for the accident.
The accident has occurred SCCH4 5 MVC No.6617/2022 since Ramaiah.S crossing the divider and entered the national highway that too during night hours.
Hence the deceased himself contributed negligence.

Further denied the age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with cost.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Ramaiah died in the Motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.11.2022 at about 7.15 p.m., near Sadahalli toll, situated at BB road, NH7 situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Chikkajala Traffic P.S.
due to the rash and negligence driving of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA40F1255 by Shivaraju.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30325063/
2 its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner prove that he is legal heirs and dependent of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
In order to prove the claim petition, petitioner No.1 himself is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Further one witness has examined as PW.2.
The respondent has examined its official as RW.1, through him got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 3.
6. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the negative.
 Issue No.3: Do not survive for  consideration,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for the  following.
 REASONS  ISSUE NO.1:
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner No.1 has filed his affidavit in lieu of chief examination, which is considered as P.W.1.

In SCCH4 7 MVC No.6617/2022 support of his claim, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar along with sketch, PM report, Inquest,
report, accident information and notice issued u/s 133 of MV Act and reply issued by owner of the vehicle.

All these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.
As per the documents, one Muniraju.S, the cousin brother of the deceased has lodged complaint with Chikkajala Traffic Police on 06.11.2022.

As per the complaint on 05.11.2022 at about 8.00 p.m., an unknown person made phone call and informed the complainant that, his brother met with an accident near Sadahalli Toll, Airport Road and he was admitted to Life Care Hospital.

Immediately the complainant came to the Hospital, after enquiry he came to know that, on 05.11.2022 at about 7.15 p.m., his brother, after finishing his work was returning to house, while so SCCH4 8 MVC No.6617/2022 coming from Sadahalli towards Devanahalli by crossing the road,
the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No. KA40F1225 came in a rash and negligent manner Shivaraju.
S vs K.S.R.T.C on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30325063/

3 with high speed and dashed to Ramaiah was crossing the road in the said accident, the said Ramaih sustained grievous injuries on his head, the publics were shifted him to nearest Life Care Hospital.
But the doctor after examining the injured declared that, he died.
Thereafter the dead body was shifted to Government Hospital, Yelahanka.
10. Upon receiving the complaint, the police have registered FIR against Rahamathulla, thereafter the police have conducted inquest.
As per the PM report the cause of death is due to head injury as a result of impact, and the injury to the head.
The injuries found on the dead body of Ramaiah are also noted in the Inquest report as well as PM report.

SCCH4 9 MVC No.6617/2022 11. The police during the investigation have visited the place of the accident and also drawn spot mahazar as well as sketch which disclose that, the accident has taken place on pedestrian cross, that too near the road median.

12. The police during the investigation have issued notice to the managing director of the respondent to furnish the documents in respect of the bus involved in the accident and who has driven the said bus at the time of the accident.
After receipt of notice the respondent has issued reply stating that, one Rahamathulla N.S. has driven the said bus at the time of the accident.
The police have also prepared the accident information report.

13. The jurisdictional police after completion of investigation have submitted charge sheet against Rahamathulla who is examined as RW1, for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A)
of IPC.
The SCCH4 10 MVC No.6617/2022 allegation made in the charge sheet as as complaint are one and the same.

14. In the written statement as well as examination in chief of RW.1, it is the defence of the respondent that, while RW.1 was driving the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA40F1255, on Bengaluru Devanahalli, NH7, near Sadahalli Toll, the deceased Ramaiah abruptly hopped over the divider, crossed over to the side of the national high way where the respondent bus moving.
Hence, RW.1 immediately applied the brakes and veered to the left in an effort to prevent the collision.
However, the deceased Ramaiah.S immediately in reverse course and rushed back, striking the bus in the process, the driver of the bud had no influence over the accident's circumstances.

The accident was beyond the control of RW.1.
SCCH4 11 MVC No.6617/2022 15.
The accident is not in dispute.
According to the respondent the accident was occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself.
As could be ascertained in the spot sketch prepared by the police, the accident has occurred near the divider of the national highway that too on pedestrian cross.
Whereas the deceased was crossing the road where there is provision for crossing the road by pedestrians, it cannot be consider that there was negligence on the part of the deceased.

Any driver of the vehicle ought to have drive the vehicle with care and caution that too near the pedestrian cross Shivaraju.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30325063/
4 one should have take much caution.
The documentary as well as oral evidence of petitioner prove that the deceased died due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA40 F1255 which belonging to the respondent.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH4 12 MVC No.6617/2022

ISSUE NO.2:
16.
As contended in the petition the petitioner is the brother of the deceased Ramaiah.S.
The petitioner to prove his relationship with deceased, has produced notarized copies Aadhar cards of himself and deceased.
These documents are marked at Ex.P.9.

During the course of evidence the original Aadhar cards are compared with the notarized copies, found correct and returned the same to the petitioners, but this document do not prove the relationship of the petitioner and the deceased.
17. Of course In the claim petition, strict proof of relationship is not necessary like in civil suit.
But there must be some primafacie material to prove that the petitioner is the brother of deceased Ramaiah.S.
There is no evidence to prove that petitioner is the brother of the deceased Ramaiah.
The petitioner without proving his relationship dependency with Ramaiah, is not entitle for SCCH4 13 MVC No.6617/2022 any compensation.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the Negative.

ISSUE No.3:
18.
In view of my finding on issue No.2, the issue No.3 do not survive for my consideration.

ISSUE No.4:
19.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
The parties shall bear their cost.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, the transcript corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 16th day of April2024)

(RAJU.M) XVIII ADDL.JUDGE Court of Small Causes & MACT., Bengaluru.
